small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs (num_warps=4/8, num_stages=3/4) and try BLOCK_OC fixed at 16 (matches OC exactly) to reduce masking overhead — current pow2 is already 16, but explicitly hoisting mask_oc-free paths when OC==BLOCK_OC helps.
- Reorder loops so the `ic` loop is the outermost and reuse the 8 spatial input loads across OC via a `tl.dot`-style inner product: load x for the 8 positions once per (kd,kh,kw,ic), then accumulate into all 8 accumulators with a single weight vector — current code already does this but the redundant address math per OC lane can be hoisted (compute base offsets once per ic/kd/kh/kw).
- Tile multiple pooled output positions per program (e.g. 2x2 in PH×PW) so weight loads amortize across more outputs; this is the biggest leverage since BLOCK_OC=16 is tiny and weight reuse is currently low.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a scatter-add ConvTranspose: one program per (N, ic, id, ih, iw) input voxel computes the (OC, KD, KH, KW) outer product and atomically accumulates into the OD×OH×OW output. Then a second small kernel does maxpool+softmax+sub+swish+channel-max. Current gather form recomputes stride-divisibility checks 27×3 times per output and only writes 1 scalar per program — very low arithmetic intensity.
- Alternative: fuse into a GEMM-style kernel where each program handles a tile of pooled output positions (BLOCK_P=8 or 16) × all OC=16 channels, performing the conv as a matmul of (OC, IC*KD*KH*KW) weight with an implicit im2col patch matrix of (IC*KD*KH*KW, BLOCK_P×POOL_K³). Weight is then reused across BLOCK_P×8 output positions instead of 8.
- Persist the pooled (N, OC, PD, PH, PW) intermediate in registers/SMEM by making one program own a full channel column at a single (n,pd,ph,pw): the softmax+sub+swish+max chain only needs 16 floats and is already trivial — the bottleneck is the conv, so any redesign should focus on weight/input reuse rather than the epilogue.
